spec_issues: The task id says 'improve-worst-seed-held-out-restoration', but every private breakdown shows a single run (seed 1009, budget_sec 600). No minimum over seeds is visible, and the overview itself says 'The grader runs the training code once'.

The overview says 'its weights must start random', but the prompt only says 'submit source code without fitted weights or learned state, and seed training from TRAIN_SEED'. Deterministic structured initialisations (identity/zero-residual in both Fable runs, Haar/phase filter banks in both GPT runs, orthogonal heads in Argon FY7nqr9) are allowed by the prompt and arguably not by the overview.

'The network's design is fixed' is enforced only by loading the weights into the pristine architecture. Zeroing whole branches keeps tensor shapes and passes that check, so functional pruning of the fixed model is possible: GPT YTBJxY3 disables the reference branch, all encoder residual blocks and most MLP channels. The spec does not say whether this is allowed.
verifier_issues: Public and private differ only in seed (public run_public.sh uses SEED=11; private uses 1009) and evaluation set (60 dev videos vs 100 hidden). The private seed never appears in any trajectory, so no agent could tune to it. All 12 submissions pass TRAIN_SEED through.

The 600 s budget is enforced by the trusted harness: sandbox.run(['bash', train.sh], ..., time.monotonic() + cfg['budget_sec']) kills the trainee process, and the last saved final.pth is scored (run_eval.py train_one, seen in gemini-3.8-flash__TyjF4sF [15]). Interpreter start-up counts against the budget. Because the budget is wall-clock, the grading host's speed changes the iteration count.
The private baseline_objective is a fixed constant (0.00047263) for every trial, so the baseline does not drift between trials.
GPT YTBJxY3 has an official reward (3.67) but an empty rewards breakdown, so its validity flags cannot be checked from public data.
task_level.noise: Run-to-run noise is small compared with most gaps. Agents measured seed spreads of std ~0.03 dB (Kimi JzJ47n2, 28 runs: 39.13 +/- 0.03), a range of 0.26 dB over 25 runs (Kimi 5m5S6zx), 0.1 dB over 3 seeds (Argon ofZBjWJ) and 0.4 dB (Gemini Flash Jmpd9jd). Near reward ~4, 0.1 dB is about 0.1 reward. The private ranking matches the agents' public dev means: Fable sQ6APHS 39.62 -> 40.10, GPT 39.28 -> 39.96/39.95, Kimi JzJ47n2 39.13 -> 39.75, Fable SdLt2sb ~38.9 -> 39.61, Argon ofZBjWJ 38.86 -> 39.58. Most trials move by +0.5 to +0.7 dB. Two outliers (Gemini Flash Jmpd9jd -0.36 dB, Grok RFTutPt +0.19 dB) show single-run variance on the graded run, but neither changes a top placement. Pairs within ~0.1 dB on the private run are coin flips: GPT 3.68 vs 3.67, Fable SdLt2sb 3.32 vs Argon ofZBjWJ 3.29, Grok RFTutPt 2.70 vs Argon FY7nqr9 2.65, and arguably Kimi JzJ47n2 3.46 vs Fable SdLt2sb 3.32. Fable's best run is about 0.14 dB above GPT privately and 0.34 dB on dev, so it is clearly best.
task_level.epoch_rationale: The scoring mechanics hold up: hidden fixed seed, hard wall-clock kill, constant baseline, and seed noise at or below ~0.1 dB, smaller than the gaps that decide the top games. One caveat is a rules question, not a measurement defect. If GPT YTBJxY3's zero-weight pruning were ruled illegal and the run zeroed, the Fable-vs-GPT game would go from 0.5 to 0.75 for Fable. Fable already holds the best single run either way.
task_level.science_vs_gaming: Almost all of the 3-7 dB gain comes from routine throughput and optimisation engineering: GPU-resident data, CUDA graphs, dropping the costly LPIPS and re-blur losses, higher LR with time-based schedules, Muon, EMA, and crop/clip-length curricula that end on the evaluation geometry. The most transferable ideas are identity-preserving structured initialisation (Haar/phase filter banks, GPT) and the finding that geometric augmentation hurts because of the Hilbert scan's orientation dependence (Fable). There is no evidence of seed tuning, dev-set fitting or budget circumvention. The one benchmark-exploiting move is GPT YTBJxY3 training a functionally pruned MambaTM inside the 'fixed' architecture, and it gained nothing over its unpruned sibling.

trials.approach: Throughput and optimiser recipe: train+val clips kept on GPU, TF32 + channels_last, a CUDA-graph-captured step (~3x the baseline iteration rate), Charbonnier loss only (LPIPS and re-blur losses dropped), Muon on matrix weights plus AdamW with Mamba blocks at 2x LR, a wall-clock warmup/constant/cosine schedule that ends at the deadline, and a 96->192 crop / 12->30 frame curriculum that ends on the evaluator's 192x192x30 tiles. A deterministic identity initialisation of a pass-through path added about +0.07 dB.

trials.approach: Same family as UYJMgrE (GPU cache, CUDA graphs, phase/identity initialisation, EMA, late switch to larger crops). The final train.sh, however, trains a functionally pruned network. '--mode partial --no_reference' zeroes and freezes the whole reference branch (ref encoder/decoder and the reference Mamba blocks); '--spatial_skip encoder_all' zeroes and bypasses every encoder residual block; '--mlp_width 256' zeroes the remaining MLP channels. Tensor shapes stay the same, so the evaluator's 'fixed' MambaTM computes a smaller network.
evidence: patch.diff train.sh: '--mode partial --regular_blocks 4 --no_reference --mlp_width 256 --spatial_skip encoder_all'

trials.approach: Five-stage resolution/length curriculum (128x128xT8 -> ... -> full 192x256x30 frames) with CUDA graphs, channels_last, fused AdamW, stretched cosine, and EMA ramp. The last 10% of training differentiates through the evaluator's 2-tile overlap averaging (0:192 / 64:256). The loss moves from Charbonnier to grayscale per-frame RMSE plus deep supervision of the LPD output, and the 3 grayscale output channels are tied at export.
